messages:
Jon K: quick heads-up — we have inconsistent semantics for omitted optional params on /v1/generate between the Python and TS SDKs. python serializes None as null; ts omits the key. server currently treats null differently in a few handlers. :grimace:
Aya L: can you paste a tiny repro?
Jon K: yep, wire examples:
```
# explicit false (curl)
POST /v1/generate
{ "prompt": "hey", "include_metadata": false }

# python sdk (None -> null)
{ "prompt": "hey", "include_metadata": null }

# ts sdk (omitted)
{ "prompt": "hey" }
```
Jon K: server unmarshal code is using a truthy/nil check that conflates missing vs null which leads to different defaulting.
Sam: that's tricky — some handlers treat null as explicit false, others use missing to apply defaults. We need a single source of truth.
Priya: what are our options? change server to treat null like missing, or change py sdk to omit None, or update contract to call out null semantics.
devbot: @Jon K opened issue #4217: "Define missing vs null semantics for inference endpoints" assigned to @dev-platform
Jon K: opened a quick python PR that changes serialization to drop keys when value is None and added tests for nested objects: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/611
Aya L: if we change the python SDK we should add a changelog entry and a migration note. Also add a golden wire test.
Sam: i'll prototype a server feature-flag: on by default keep current behavior but log when null is received; add a switch to treat null as missing after a 2-week canary. That lets us roll safely.
Priya: agree. also add an integration test that validates that py/ts payloads result in the same effective behavior (defaults + opt-outs). add to sdk-interop job.
Jon K: +1. I'll add a pact-style test that asserts canonical wire payloads for a set of common requests nightly.
infra-bot: test-plan: add e2e: sdk-interop (python, typescript) -> staging endpoint -> compare effective response; add a golden serialization job.
Jon K: FYI there's a related enum bug: python sending null for optional enum triggers a 400 in some server parsers; ts undefined is fine. I'll include that case in the PR tests.
Sam: i'll add server-side unit tests for enum unmarshal and ensure we return 422 with a clear error if a client explicitly sends null for a non-nullable enum. For optional enums we should treat null as missing only after the migration window.
Priya: timeline proposal: python SDK PR today -> run unit + sdk-interop tests -> server feature-flag PR tomorrow -> enable logs in staging -> 2-week canary -> flip flag -> doc update and deprecation note.
Jon K: can someone review the python PR? pinging reviewers.
Priya: i'll take first pass and leave comments. :eyes:
Sam: i'll review server patch in the morning and add the feature-flag.
Aya L: i'll draft a short section in API contract docs that defines semantics for: missing, null, explicit false, and how defaults are applied. will post in #docs for review.
Jon K: one more ask — add a regression test in the nightly CI that serializes known inputs from both sdks and compares wire payloads. if mismatch, fail and notify SDK owners.
infra-bot: created job sdk-wire-golden with triggers: nightly + on-sdk-publish
ops-bot: deploybot: feature-flag branch queued for staging at 2024-10-11T18:40:00Z
Jon K: thanks — will run the integration harness after staging deploy lands. :pray:
